title: A smooth morphism has standard-smooth affine charts of its relative dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of pure relative dimension $d$. For every $x\in X$ there are affine open neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $f(x)$, with $f(V)\subseteq T$, such that the ring map $R\to A$ of $f|_V$ is standard smooth of relative dimension $d$, i.e. $A$ has a standard smooth presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] whose relative dimension $n-c$ equals $d$.

source.place: Tags 02G2 (Definition: smooth of relative dimension d) and 054L (etale-local normal form)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-locally-standard-smooth] to $f$ at $x$: there are affine opens $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $x\in V$, $f(V)\subseteq T$ and $R\to A$ the ring map of $f|_V$, such that $A$ is standard smooth over $R$. Choose a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] with $n\ge c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{A/R}$ is a free $A$-module of rank $n-c$.

By hypothesis $f$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] applies: $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ is locally free of constant rank $d$, and its restriction to the affine pair $V\subseteq X$, $T\subseteq S$ is the sheaf associated with $\Omega_{A/R}$, which by Step 1 is $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus(n-c)}$. Hence there is an open $U\subseteq V$ containing $x$ with $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus d}\cong\Omega^1_{X/S}|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n-c)}$; taking the stalk at $x$ and tensoring with $\kappa(x)$ gives $\kappa(x)^{d}\cong\kappa(x)^{n-c}$, so $n-c=d$. Thus the presentation of Step 1 has relative dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], which is the claim.

proof_origin.place: Morphisms, Lemmas 01V7 and 02G1, with Algebra, Definition 00T6 and Lemma 00T7(2)
